blank. She lived as though she were entirely alone,
needing no one. Ella, one of the primary women
in town, explicitly says she junked Sethy
because Seth was too prideful.
Too prideful. Yeah. Sethy's fierce
self-sufficiency was read by the community as an arrogant
rejection of them. She acted like she didn't need
their forgiveness. I see.
So, the ledger between 124 and the town wasn't
just unbalanced because of the town's jealousy.
There was a massive, stubborn, calcified debt of
pride on both sides.
Denver walking to Lady Jones's house and asking for
a job, asking for food.
That was the first payment on that debt in
18 years. It broke the stalemate.
The community finally steps in to audit the haunting,
proving the ledger can't be balanced alone.
You cannot survive this kind of trauma in isolation.
No, you can't. And it's crucial to remember where
the community learned this collective power in the first
place. They didn't invent it on the spot.
They learned it from baby Suggs, whose greatest act
was reaccounting the value of the human body itself.
We have to talk about the clearing.
Oh, absolutely. This is perhaps the beating
heart of the entire novel.

in a wide open place cut deep in

She has a twisted hip.

of labor, And she bangs her walking stick on
